note: One scenario per walk. `expect` is the DOCUMENT's answer, not the driver's: the stage order, the visits, the crossings, the end state and the parks are read off bundle.json. `verdicts` is the decider's policy, one outcome per visit of the stage it names — the bench writes the gate's record only after the row has parked on it.

scenarios.title: stage the draft and hand it on
scenarios.about: A sequence handoff: the first stage stages the work, the second receives it, and the row finishes on the last stage's own verdict because its artifact is not a pull request.

scenarios.title: route an accepting review
scenarios.about: The review settles with no record, so the row parks on G1; the decider writes accept and the document routes H-02 on to publish. Nothing bounces.

scenarios.title: route a rejecting review, then an accepting one
scenarios.about: The first review rejects: the row bounces along H-03 to a second draft, is reviewed again, and the second review accepts on to publish. One gate, both outcomes, one bounce.

scenarios.title: wait behind a live row, then start
scenarios.about: The pipeline is filed behind a row that is already running. Three sweeps of the panel's clock must leave it queued with no stage started; when the live row settles, the pipeline starts and walks to done.

blocker.title: a row that is already running

scenarios.title: ping-pong until the cap stops it
scenarios.about: Both edges are capped loops, so the two-way ping-pong must spend two crossings each and park on H-01's cap. Anything past five starts, or a park that names no cap, is the loop this document exists to catch.
